A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ParaStep study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched despite relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original latency and generation-quality experiments across image, video, and audio models, including scalability studies and appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds SVD latency breakdowns and comparisons with DeepCache in Tables 5 and 7.

M1.justification: The reuse-then-predict procedure, warm-up, BatchStep, TeaCache integration, and Appendix A algorithm remain unchanged. Appendix C newly describes text-encoder partitioning, without establishing a revision to the proposed denoising algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same image, video, and audio tasks using MS-COCO, VBench, and AudioCaps, including HunyuanVideo in the appendix. The added experiments use the existing SVD task and introduce no new data or task coverage.

E2.justification: DeepCache, previously discussed only as related work, becomes an evaluated SVD comparator in v2 Appendix E.3 and Table 7. Existing comparisons with AsyncDiff, xDiT-Pipe, xDiT-Ring, and TeaCache are retained.

E3.justification: v2 adds separate computation and communication timing measurements and an additional 50-step SVD comparison specifying EulerDiscreteScheduler and DeepCache intervals of 2, 4, 6, and 8. The previously reported experimental settings remain unchanged; the additions do not establish that earlier experiments were revised.

E4.justification: New Section 5.4 examines whether communication costs explain SVD speedups by separating computation and communication latency. Existing warm-up sensitivity, scalability, TeaCache integration, and qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The new checklist states that random seeds are controlled across models and methods and explicitly answers no to statistical-significance reporting. This adds seed-control disclosure, but no repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Existing tables and plotted results are unchanged, including v1 Table 5 becoming v2 Table 6. New Table 5 reports communication times of 0.10/0.14 seconds for ParaStep versus 8.59/10.29 for AsyncDiff at p=2/4, and Table 7 adds SVD caching comparisons. These are additional results, not demonstrated improvements over v1 under matched conditions.

T1.justification: The diffusion and flow-matching equations, relative-MAE definition, communication-volume derivations, and warm-up speedup bound are retained. The checklist references existing derivations without adding mathematical assumptions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about communication-efficient parallel denoising, generation quality, multimodal applicability, and BatchStep. The headline speedups are unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix C narrows the replication-related memory limitation from the entire model to the noise predictor and explains how partitioning the text encoder can reduce memory use. New discussion attributes measured speedups to communication savings and interprets the resource-quality tradeoff against DeepCache.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link, states that its README provides setup and usage instructions, discloses 946 VBench samples, and describes text-encoder placement. These are documentation additions; the PDFs do not establish a changed sample count or independently verify repository contents.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Training-free adaptive diffusion with bounded difference approximation strategy and Accelerating diffusion transformers with token-wise feature caching. The new DeepCache comparison also modestly extends positioning against single-device acceleration, while the main related-work discussion remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most scientific prose is retained. v2 inserts the performance-breakdown subsection and appendix comparison, expands the limitations discussion, updates affiliation and conference text, and adds acknowledgments and a NeurIPS checklist without substantially restructuring the narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 5 and 7, renumbers the HunyuanVideo table, relocates existing tables and figures, and expands Figure 3's caption. Existing plotted images, qualitative examples, and method diagrams remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the measured latency breakdown, additional DeepCache comparison, and reproducibility disclosures modestly strengthen the paper's evidence and usability. The benefit is limited by an overbroad new claim of consistent quality superiority: Table 7 reports PSNR 24.9949 for ParaStep p=4 versus 26.4912 for DeepCache s=4, despite ParaStep's lower latency. Statistical uncertainty also remains unquantified.
